mainTopic: Mixtures of fit and blemished limbs: רבי אליעזר's source in 'מום בם', the dispute in the משנה about offering the remaining limbs, and the start of the משנה on blood mixed with other liquids.
overview: The amud opens by asking why רבי אליעזר lets limbs of a בעל מום that got mixed with fit limbs go on the מזבח. רב הונא says it is a tiny eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא. That fails, because רבי עקיבא allowed it only after the fact. רב פפא's attempt to save it with the כבש also fails. So the גמרא gives a new reason from the פסוק 'מום בם': a blemish hidden in a mixture does not reject the animal. The רבנן learn a different rule from those words, that a healed blemish is accepted. רבי אליעזר learns that rule from 'בם' versus 'בהם'. רבי אליעזר's words 'I view it as wood' turn out to be an argument aimed at the רבנן. The רבנן reply that blemished flesh is repulsive, unlike חטאת flesh. A new משנה follows about fit limbs mixed with blemished ones. רבי אלעזר says רבי אליעזר allows the remaining limbs only in pairs, and 'one' in the משנה means one pair. Finally, a new משנה begins on sacred blood mixed with water, wine, or ordinary blood.

steps.title: רב הונא: it is a small eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that רבי אליעזר means a minor blemish on the eye. He holds like רבי עקיבא, who says such limbs stay on the מזבח once they are brought up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: רבי אליעזר is talking about small blemishes on the eye. He follows רבי עקיבא, who said: if they went up, they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it raised before: why is a blemished animal different? רב הונא says the blemish is only a tiny one on the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish on the eye is very minor and is not a disgrace to the מזבח. רבי עקיבא already said that limbs with such a blemish stay on the מזבח once they are brought up. So רב הונא ties רבי אליעזר's ruling to that opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Small spots or blemishes on the eye
According to the opinion of
If they went up on the מזבח, they do not come down

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is talking about small blemishes on the eye,
and it follows the opinion of Rabbi Akiva,
who said: if they went up, they do not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of why a בעל מום is treated differently from other disqualified animals.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a minor blemish, plus linking it to an existing opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think any blemished animal could be offered in a mixture.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a minor eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא's rule that such limbs stay on the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא only allowed it after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי עקיבא only said such limbs may stay up if they were already brought up. He never said you may offer them in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say רבי עקיבא said this when it was already done. Did he say you may do it in the first place?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. רבי עקיבא's rule was only after the fact, but רבי אליעזר allows offering the mixture from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a big difference between 'if it already happened, leave it' and 'go ahead and do it.' רבי אליעזר lets the כהן offer all the limbs from the start. So רבי עקיבא's after-the-fact rule cannot be his source.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was already done (after the fact)
In the first place, from the start
Did he say? (a challenge meaning: he did not say)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real question asking for information. 'מִי אָמַר' is a challenge, meaning 'he never said that!'

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – דְּאִי עֲבַד;
phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Akiva said it when it was already done;
did he say it in the first place?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's link to רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that רבי אליעזר follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא allowed it only after the fact, but רבי אליעזר allows it from the start.

steps.title: רב פפא: the limbs were already brought up the ramp
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the case is one where all the limbs were already carried up the כבש. That counts as 'after the fact.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What case are we dealing with here? Where they were already brought up onto the ramp.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends רב הונא. He says the limbs were already on the ramp of the מזבח, so this is already an after-the-fact situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once limbs are on the כבש, it is as if they already 'went up.' So רבי עקיבא's after-the-fact rule would fit. This answers the challenge of לכתחלה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where they went up onto the ramp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 2 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is offering the limbs from the very start.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limbs were already on the כבש, so it is after the fact.

steps.title: Then even unmixed limbs should be offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if being on the כבש is enough, then even limbs that are not mixed up should be offered. So why does the ברייתא need a mixture?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even when they are on their own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב פפא's answer. If the כבש makes it after the fact, the mixture would not matter at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's rule works for any limbs with a minor blemish that went up, even ones that are not mixed. But the ברייתא clearly makes the mixture the key point. So this explanation misses what the ברייתא is about.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
As they are, on their own (not mixed)

phrases.english: If so, then even when they are on their own!
phrases.notes: He means: on their own, without being mixed with kosher limbs, they should also be offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer and ends the רב הונא approach.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's answer about the כבש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the כבש makes it after the fact, the mixture becomes pointless, but the משנה makes the mixture the reason.

steps.title: New reason: the verse says the blemish must be 'in them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier approach. It says רבי אליעזר learns from the פסוק 'מום בם' that a blemished animal is rejected only when the blemish is clearly in it, not when it is hidden in a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אליעזר's reason is: the תורה limited it with 'a blemish is in them.' Only then are they not accepted. But through a mixture, they are accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a brand new reason for רבי אליעזר, based on a פסוק. This explains why only a מום works this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מום בם' are read as a limit: the animal is rejected only when its blemish is clearly 'in them.' Once it is lost in a mixture, it is accepted. Since this limit is written only about a מום, it does not help other disqualified animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier answer)
The Torah limited it, excluded a case
A blemish is in them
They will be accepted (as offerings)
A mixture

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why רבי אליעזר treats a מום differently from other problems: the special limit in the פסוק is written only about a מום.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Eliezer's reason is:
the Merciful One limited it with 'a blemish is in them' –
only then are they not accepted,
but through a mixture – they are accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the רב הונא approach, which was knocked down in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's rule depends on רבי עקיבא's after-the-fact rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר learns it from 'מום בם': a blemish hidden in a mixture does not reject the animal.

steps.title: How the רבנן read the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'מום בם' for a different teaching: only while the blemish is still there is the animal rejected. Once the blemish has gone away, it is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Only while 'a blemish is in them' are they not accepted. But once the blemish has passed, they are accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree with רבי אליעזר, read 'מום בם.' They learn something else from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, 'בם' means 'still in them right now.' So an animal whose blemish healed can be accepted. They do not learn anything about mixtures from these words.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who disagree with רבי אליעזר
The blemish has passed (healed)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The question is short: how do the רבנן read 'מום בם' if they don't learn mixtures from it?

phrases.english: Only while 'a blemish is in them' are they not accepted,
but if the blemish has passed – they are accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבנן's use of the same words that רבי אליעזר used in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the רבנן learn from 'מום בם'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That a blemish which has healed no longer rejects the animal.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns the healed-blemish rule from בם versus בהם
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns the healed-blemish rule from the change between 'בם' and 'בהם' in the פסוק. The רבנן do not learn anything from that change.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר learns it from 'בם' versus 'בהם.' And the רבנן do not learn anything from 'בם' versus 'בהם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי אליעזר gets the healed-blemish rule, since he used 'מום בם' for mixtures. It also says the רבנן do not learn from this wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says 'משחתם בהם' (the longer word) and also 'מום בם' (the shorter word). רבי אליעזר learns an extra teaching from the longer word. The רבנן see no meaning in the different wording, so they need 'מום בם' for the healed-blemish rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Two forms of 'in them,' a short one and a long one
They do not learn anything from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: 'מום בם' teaches that a blemished animal hidden in a mixture is accepted, and 'בם/בהם' teaches that a healed blemish is accepted. רבנן: 'מום בם' teaches only the healed-blemish rule, and they learn nothing from 'בם/בהם.'

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer learns it from 'bam' versus 'bahem',
phrases.notes: The same פסוק says 'משחתם בהם' and also 'מום בם'. The longer word gives him the healed-blemish rule.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis do not learn anything from 'bam' versus 'bahem'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the loop by giving רבי אליעזר a separate source for the רבנן's teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both sides agree a healed blemish is accepted. They differ only on whether 'בם/בהם' teaches anything, which frees up 'מום בם' for רבי אליעזר's mixture rule.

steps.title: Why say 'I view it as wood' if the תורה already permits it?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר learns from 'מום בם' that blemished limbs in a mixture are fit, why does he need to say he 'views' them as wood?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does he say 'I view it'? The Merciful One already made it fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from the previous steps. If the תורה itself permits blemished limbs that are mixed in, רבי אליעזר's 'I view the flesh as wood' sounds unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי אליעזר said he 'views' the blemished flesh as if it were wood. But according to step 5, he holds the פסוק 'מום בם' makes mixed blemished limbs fully fit. Something that is fully fit does not need to be treated as wood, so the wording seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is true
I view, I look at it as if
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Made it fit or valid

phrases.english: If so, why say "I view"?!
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אליעזר's earlier words: 'I view the flesh as if it were wood.'

phrases.english: But the Merciful One made it fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'מום בם' explanation by pointing to רבי אליעזר's own wording
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's phrase 'I view the flesh as wood'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תורה makes the mixed blemished limbs fully fit, there is no need to treat them as wood.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר was arguing from the רבנן's own view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tells the רבנן: I hold the תורה permits it, but even you should agree it is at least like wood, just as with חטאת flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He spoke to them according to their own view. For me, the Merciful One made it fit. For you, at least admit to me that the flesh of a blemished animal is like wood, just like the flesh of a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'I view it as wood' was not רבי אליעזר's own reason. He was making an extra argument to the רבנן using their own position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's real reason is the פסוק 'מום בם.' But he also argues that even if the רבנן do not accept that, they already agree that חטאת flesh mixed with עולה flesh can go on the מזבח as if it were wood. So they should say the same about blemished flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words, arguing from the other side's view
According to me / according to you
At least admit to me
Just like, the same as
The meat of a sin offering

phrases.english: He is speaking to them according to their own words:
According to me, the Merciful One made it fit;
according to you, at least admit to me
that the flesh of a blemished animal is like wood,
just like the flesh of a sin offering!
phrases.notes: He means the case where חטאת meat got mixed with עולה meat. There the רבנן agree it all goes up, with the חטאת treated like wood.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the wording is an argument based on the other side's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'I view it as wood' looked like רבי אליעזר's own reason, which would be unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is an extra argument aimed at the רבנן; his own reason is the פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not really think the blemished flesh is only 'wood.' For himself it is fully fit. The 'wood' idea is only to convince the רבנן.

steps.title: The רבנן: blemished flesh is repulsive
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that blemished flesh is repulsive, so it cannot go up even as wood, unlike חטאת flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Here the limbs are repulsive; there they are not repulsive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן answer רבי אליעזר's comparison, and gives their reply in a few words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן separate the two cases. חטאת meat is fine in itself, so it can go on the מזבח as wood. Blemished meat is repulsive for the מזבח, so it cannot go up even as wood.

keyTerms.meaning: They are repulsive, disgusting
Here / there

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר permits blemished limbs in a mixture because of 'מום בם.' The רבנן do not learn this from the פסוק. They also reject the 'wood' argument, because blemished flesh is repulsive and cannot go up even as wood, unlike חטאת flesh.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, how do they answer?
Here they are repulsive; there they are not repulsive.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן – הָכָא מְאִיסִי, הָתָם לָא מְאִיסִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's response to רבי אליעזר's comparison in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן deal with the comparison to חטאת flesh
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blemished flesh is repulsive; חטאת flesh is not, so the cases differ.

steps.title: New משנה: fit limbs mixed with blemished limbs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר: once one head or one set of legs is offered, all the rest of that kind may be offered. חכמים: even if only one is left, it goes to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Limbs mixed with limbs of blemished animals. רבי אליעזר says: if the head of one of them was offered, all the heads may be offered. If the legs of one of them were offered, all the legs may be offered. And חכמים say: even if all were offered except one, that one goes out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a dispute about what to do when fit limbs get mixed up with limbs of blemished animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר is lenient: once one head is offered, we can say that was the blemished one, so the rest may be offered. חכמים are strict: as long as even one limb is left, it might be the blemished one, so it must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Limbs of an animal offering
Animals with a blemish, unfit for the מזבח
Legs
The place in the עזרה where unfit offerings are burned

phrases.english: MISHNA
Limbs that got mixed with limbs of blemished animals:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
if the head of one of them was offered,
all the heads shall be offered.
If the legs of one of them were offered,
all the legs shall be offered.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ קָרְבוּ כֻּלָּם חוּץ מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: even if all of them were offered except for one of them,
it must go out to the place of burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: after one head or set of legs is offered, the rest may be offered. חכמים: as long as any limb remains, it must be burned.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: only two at a time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר limits רבי אליעזר's leniency: the remaining limbs may be offered only in pairs, not one by one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אלעזר said: רבי אליעזר only allowed them two at a time, but not one at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה with רבי אלעזר's limit on how רבי אליעזר's leniency works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two heads are offered together, at least one is surely fit. Offering one alone might mean offering the blemished one by itself, so רבי אלעזר says רבי אליעזר did not allow that.

keyTerms.meaning: Two at a time, in pairs
One at a time, singly
He permitted, ruled it fit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אלעזר, who is speaking here, with רבי אליעזר, whose view in the משנה he is explaining.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabbi Elazar said:
Rabbi Eliezer did not permit
except two at a time,
but one at a time, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר permits offering the remaining limbs only in pairs, not singly.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the משנה talks about one last limb
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה objects: חכמים forbid even the one last limb, which suggests רבי אליעזר permits offering a single limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objected: and חכמים say, even if all were offered except one, it goes out to the place of burning!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי אלעזר using the words of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים talk about a case where only one limb is left. They seem to be arguing with רבי אליעזר about that same case, so רבי אליעזר must allow even one last limb to be offered alone. That goes against רבי אלעזר's 'two at a time only' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for one

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised an objection:
"And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ קָרְבוּ כּוּלָּן חוּץ מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: even if all of them were offered except for one of them,
it must go out to the place of burning!"
phrases.notes: His point: if חכמים say this about the last single limb, רבי אליעזר must disagree and allow it, even though it is just one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's limit from step 12 using the משנה in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's rule that רבי אליעזר allows only two at a time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חכמים argue about the very last single limb, which shows רבי אליעזר allows offering a single limb.

steps.title: One means one pair
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא explains that the word 'one' in the משנה means 'one pair,' so the challenge falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא said to him: I will explain it to you. What does 'one' mean? It means one pair.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא answers רבי ירמיה's question from the last step. He says the word 'one' in the משנה really means 'one pair.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה thought the חכמים saying 'even one' showed that רבי אליעזר allows a single limb. But if 'one' means one pair, the חכמים are only arguing about the last pair. So רבי אלעזר's rule that limbs go up only in pairs still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you
one pair (two limbs together)
what (does it mean)?

steps.whatToRemember: In this משנה, the 'one' that is left over means one pair of limbs. Even רבי אליעזר allows offering the limbs only in pairs, not one by one. חכמים say even the last pair must be burned.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Taḥlifa said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי ירמיה, who asked the question in the step before.

phrases.english: I will explain it to you:
What is 'one'? One pair.
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to the חכמים's words in the משנה: 'even if all were offered except for one.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ מַאי אֶחָד זוּג אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge from step 13 and protects רבי אלעזר's rule from step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים's phrase 'even one' suggests that רבי אליעזר allowed offering a single limb.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One' means one pair. Limbs are offered only in pairs, even according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Sacred blood mixed with water, wine, or animal blood
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: sacred blood mixed with water is fit if it still looks like blood. When it is mixed with wine or with ordinary animal blood, we picture the added liquid as water.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Blood that got mixed with water is fit, if the mixture still looks like blood. If it got mixed with wine, we view the wine as if it were water. If it got mixed with the blood of a בהמה or a חיה, we view that blood as if it were water.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic. It deals with sacred blood that got mixed into another liquid before the זריקה on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the mixture still looks like blood. Wine and ordinary blood are red, so you cannot judge them by how the mixture looks. Instead, we imagine that much clear water in their place and ask whether the mixture would still look like blood.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (a new משנה starts here)
the look of blood
fit (here, fit for זריקה on the מזבח)
we view it as if it were water
blood of a tame animal and blood of a wild animal (here, ordinary non-sacred blood)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אותו' (it) in 'we view it as water' is the wine or the ordinary blood, not the sacred blood. The sacred blood stays as it is. We only picture the added liquid as water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general way to judge mixtures. When the added liquid looks like the main one, we judge it by imagining it as something that looks different, like water.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood mixed with water is fit if it still looks like blood. Wine or ordinary animal blood mixed in is judged as if it were water.
